- When sentiment is negative or neutral in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for such periods.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above prior peak.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., >0.67 for 3+ consecutive days), model tends to overreact; apply downward bias of 1–3% to prevent overcorrection.
- Mean reversion is evident in 3–5 day horizons: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, adjust downward by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates downward moves after negative sentiment; add 1–3% buffer for downside risk when sentiment <0.3.
- If sentiment is mixed or volatile (alternating 0.00/1.00), model exhibits erratic behavior; use median of last 5 days as anchor for correction.
